title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page compares the budgets and revenues of the films through scatterplot. In Figure 1, scatterplot shows whether budget size results in increased revenue size.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget")
plt.ylabel("Revenue")
plt.title("Budget vs. Revenue")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Relationship between budget and revenue for movies in dataset

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
This page compares whether longer films have higher IMDb ratings. In Figure 1, the scatter plot compares each film’s runtime with its rating.
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb Rating")
plt.title("Runtime vs. IMDb Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Relationship between film runtime and IMDb rating

title: Bond Films
text:
This page looks at how the revenue of James Bond films changed over time. In Figure 1, it shows the revenue of each Bond film by release year.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")


plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Release Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (million USD)")
plt.title("James Bond Revenue Over Time")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide revenue of James Bond films over time





The first James Bond film in dataset was released in 1995, and last was released in 2021.
